status_summary: ONDCP's drug policy priorities released on 2025-04-03 list reducing overdose deaths with a focus on fentanyl first, followed by supply chain, border, prevention, treatment and research. The HALT Fentanyl Act (Public Law 119-26) was approved on 2025-07-16, and Executive Order 14367 of 2025-12-15 designated illicit fentanyl a weapon of mass destruction. The 2026 National Drug Control Strategy, released on 2026-05-04, covers prevention, treatment and supply reduction, but its fact sheet does not rank goals, opens with border interdiction and cartels and places overdose response last. No document was found describing the Director's consultation with border officials.

timeline.event: ONDCP released the administration's six drug policy priorities, led by reducing overdose deaths with a focus on fentanyl.
The HALT Fentanyl Act became Public Law 119-26, placing fentanyl-related substances in Schedule I as a class.
Executive Order 14367 designated illicit fentanyl and core precursors as weapons of mass destruction and assigned enforcement tasks to Justice, State, Treasury, War and Homeland Security.
The Senate confirmed Sara Carter as ONDCP Director by a 52 to 48 vote.

A presidential document dated this day describes the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, set up by the Secretary of War as a pledge by military leaders and representatives of 17 countries, with goals including dismantling cartels designated as foreign terrorist organizations.
ONDCP released the 2026 National Drug Control Strategy; its fact sheet covers prevention, treatment and supply reduction, opens with border interdiction and cartels and places overdose response last.

State published the foreign terrorist organization designation of the Juarez Cartel and Los Viagras under section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, effective on publication (signed 2026-07-02).

title: Make fentanyl and overdoses the top drug policy priority; consult border officials
uncertainties: The full strategy document was not opened; its contents were judged from the official fact sheet, which does not rank goals. Overdose death trends were not examined.
